When Cristiano Ronaldo descended upon Riyadh in January 2023, the footballing landscape shifted on its axis. Yet, the true legacy of his historic move to the Gulf may not be written in the goals he scores for Al-Nassr, but in the legal templates he is breaking. For decades, the Gulf kingdoms maintained an unyielding wall between foreign residents and permanent status. Expatriates entered on strict work permits, tied entirely to their employers, and departed the moment their contracts expired.Today, Ronaldo operates in an entirely different reality. He owns a piece of the kingdom. Without holding a Saudi passport, the Portuguese icon has secured the right to buy land, sponsor his family, and anchor his post-football life in the country. This unprecedented arrangement is made possible by a highly sophisticated legal instrument: Saudi Arabia’s Gifted Residency programme.Ronaldo’s arrival on January 3, 2023, set a staggering benchmark for luxury. He and his extensive entourage initially commandeered 17 suites at the Four Seasons Hotel Riyadh at Kingdom Centre. For a month, the family resided in the two-story Kingdom Suite, a sprawling 4,000-square-foot duplex suspended between the 48th and 50th floors, costing an estimated $300,000.However, a hotel, no matter how grand, is not a home. The family soon transitioned to an exclusive, heavily fortified residential compound in Riyadh’s Al Muhammadiyah district. This estate serves as their principal base and comes as a phenomenal, club-provided perk. Al-Nassr handles the estate completely, funding a dedicated 16-person staff that operates like a boutique luxury hotel. The operation includes three drivers, four housemaids, two private chefs, three gardeners, and four security guards protecting the family 24/7. To supplement his life in the capital, the club also provided Ronaldo with a private jet valued at €4.5 million, covering all operational costs.Following his contract extension in June 2025, which binds him to Al-Nassr until 2027, and his marriage to Georgina Rodríguez in a private civil ceremony in Portugal on August 11, 2026, Riyadh has cemented itself as the family's geographic anchor.While Al-Nassr provides his palatial Riyadh compound, Ronaldo’s long-term legal security rests on theFirst introduced in 2019 under Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s Vision 2030 framework, the initiative was significantly expanded in January 2024 to include specialized tracks. Among these, the Gifted Residency was designed explicitly for elite international talent, athletes, and cultural pioneers.The government rolled out these pathways with explicit macro-economic goals: driving economic diversification away from oil dependency, accelerating the growth of the local sports and tourism sectors, and positioning the kingdom as a global hub that directly attracts and integrates world-class elite talent, innovators, and cultural pioneers into the country's long-term future.Under normal circumstances, foreign players in the Saudi Pro League receive a standard athlete work visa. This traditional route leaves them legally dependent on their club as a(employer sponsor). If a player is transferred, retired, or dropped, their visa is voided, and they must exit the country or find a new employer.The Gifted Residency completely flips this dynamic. Endorsed directly by the Ministry of Sports, Ronaldo’s residency functions entirely independent of Al-Nassr. It grants a distinct set of structural privileges:The most profound benefit of the Gifted Residency is the absolute right to own freehold real estate. Ronaldo put this mechanism into action by looking beyond the capital to the pristine sands of the Red Sea coast, acquiring two ultra-luxury villas at Nujuma, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve.Reported at an estimated combined cost of £7 million ($9 million), the purchase establishes Ronaldo and Georgina as some of the very first individual owners within the hyper-exclusive Red Sea Residences community. The development features just 19 standalone, ocean-ring-shaped villas situated on private islands roughly 26 kilometres from the mainland. The estate is accessible exclusively via chartered boat or seaplane.Crucially, the sheer scale of this transactional value highlights a fascinating crossover in Saudi immigration law. Even if Cristiano Ronaldo were not a famed global footballing superstar, this purchase alone would have automatically granted him a Premium Residency. Under the program's official Real Estate Owner pathway, any foreign national who acquires developed, unmortgaged residential property valued at SAR 4 million (approximately $1.07 million USD) or more is legally entitled to long-term residency privileges. By spending $9 million, Ronaldo cleared this statutory benchmark nearly nine times over. Had he entered the country as an anonymous, ultra-high-net-worth investor rather than the world's most recognizable athlete, the doors of the Premium Residency Center would have swung open just as wide.The couple acquired a three-bedroom villa designed for primary family use alongside a separate two-bedroom villa. The island features world-class amenities including the Neyrah Spa, the Galaxea Diving Center, and a dedicated Conservation House. Reflecting on the sanctuary, Ronaldo shared his experience in verbatim terms reported by theRonaldo’s property footprint is part of a broader, dual-pronged strategy in the Gulf. In February 2020, he was awarded the UAE Golden Visa by the Dubai Sports Council. Granted under the "elite talent" and "sports creators" category, the 10-year residency allowed him to bypass traditional property investment thresholds entirely based on his sporting prestige. As part of that inaugural cohort alongside stars like Novak Djokovic, the UAE utilized Ronaldo to pioneer its own specialized talent track.He would later leverage this long-term legal security to expand his regional footprint into premium Dubai real estate, reportedly purchasing a luxury waterfront property on Jumeirah Bay Island in 2024 for an estimated €25 million to €30 million—though that landmark transaction came years after his Golden Visa was initially awarded.The Saudi Gifted Residency operates on a parallel plane but offers a tailored level of local authority. John Pagano, CEO of Red Sea International, noted that Ronaldo's entry into the Red Sea community highlights a shared ethos. The entire destination operates on radical environmental goals, aiming for a 30% net positive ecological impact by 2040. Powered entirely by renewable energy, the community sits within three hours of 250 million people via the new Red Sea International Airport.Through the intersection of sports diplomacy and legislative reform, Saudi Arabia has given its premier football icon something far more valuable than a record-breaking salary: a permanent, sovereign stake in the kingdom's future.
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo moved to Saudi Arabia in January 2023. He and his family live in a four-storey, $300,000-a-year palace. He has the right to stay in the country until he retires in 2027.

Article Title: Neymar sent off for breaking ‘Vini Jr. rule’ after mouth-covering exchange, opponent claims disrespect, Santos star fires back in furious rant
Article Text:
Soccer Football - Brasileiro Championship - Santos v Coritiba - Neo Quimica Arena, Sao Paulo, Brazil - May 17, 2026 Santos' Neymar reacts REUTERS/Jean Carniel

Why Neymar was shown a straight red card

What Rodrigo Nestor said about Neymar

Neymar apologises to Santos fans before launching angry attack

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Neymar was sent off in Santos’ 1-1 draw with Bahia after covering his mouth during a heated exchange with Rodrigo Nestor, prompting a VAR review and a straight red card under the so-called “Vini Jr. rule”. The Brazilian forward later admitted he had made a mistake but fiercely accused his opponent of exploiting an anti-racism measure to gain an advantage, launching an angry attack on the Bahia midfielder on social media.The incident unfolded before the second half began on Saturday, October 24, with Santos trailing 1-0. It followed an earlier confrontation between the pair and a half-time television interview in which Nestor accused Neymar of disrespecting him and Bahia. Santos eventually rescued a 1-1 draw, but the controversy surrounding their captain quickly overshadowed the result.The tension between Neymar and Nestor had been building throughout the first half. After a foul, Neymar threw the ball towards the Bahia midfielder, prompting a confrontation involving players from both sides. Neymar received a yellow card for his part in the incident.The dispute continued during the interval. As the teams gathered near the centre circle ahead of the restart, Neymar approached Nestor and appeared to exchange words with him.After initially laughing, the Santos forward returned to the conversation with his hand covering his mouth.Nestor immediately alerted the referee, Sávio Pereira Sampaio. Following a review of the footage at the pitchside monitor, the official showed Neymar a straight red card before the second half could begin. The decision was made under the rule commonly referred to as the “Vini Jr. rule”, which targets players who cover their mouths while allegedly directing abusive or discriminatory remarks at opponents.The measure is intended to help officials address abuse that might otherwise be concealed from cameras and spectators. Covering one's mouth alone does not establish what was said, but in this incident the referee acted after reviewing the footage and applying the relevant rule.Neymar reacted furiously to the dismissal. The confrontation continued as he left the field, with players and staff from both teams becoming involved in the ensuing commotion. Reports also described Neymar moving towards Nestor before others intervened.Nestor had already explained his side of the dispute during a half-time interview with Brazilian broadcaster SporTV. He accused Neymar of making disrespectful remarks and said he would not repeat them publicly."My parents raised me well, I'm very grateful to them," he said, as reported by Marca. "And I know perfectly well where I come from. I was born in Itaquera; it was difficult to get where I am today, and I'm proud to wear the Bahia jersey."He knows what he said to me. It was disrespectful to me and to the Bahia jersey. He's an idol to everyone as a player, but today he failed as a person because of the way he spoke. You shouldn't do those kinds of things. My parents raised me very well, and I'm grateful for the upbringing they gave me. I would never say something like that."Nestor declined to disclose the precise words he claimed Neymar had used, explaining that children were watching the broadcast. Neymar, however, would later dispute Nestor's account of what happened during their exchange.After the match, Neymar addressed the controversy in a series of Instagram Stories. He apologised to Santos supporters and congratulated his team for fighting back to earn a draw, but he also questioned the use of the rule and accused Nestor of acting dishonestly.Neymar admitted that covering his mouth had been a mistake, while maintaining that he had not said anything to warrant the dismissal."What Nestor did to me today is very serious. Serious because this is a rule created to combat racism. He tried to gain an advantage in the game because I put my hand over my mouth, and I didn't even say anything to him. Obviously, we were trading insults, taking digs at each other, and that's fine, it's part of football."He continued: "But what he did is very serious. I was in midfield, we were joking around and arguing, I was joking with the two center-backs, and he used that to gain an advantage in the game. If this is a rule created to combat racism, how can he do these things? It's surreal."Neymar then accused Nestor of deliberately misrepresenting the exchange."I'm really upset about what happened because he was so underhanded. Really, really underhanded. I saw an interview where he said I'd insulted him, that he couldn't repeat it because there were kids watching. Man, he faked it. I threw the ball at his waist, and he put his hand to his face. And what kind of example does he think he's setting?"He also acknowledged his own role in the incident before directing another insult at his opponent."I had the chance to do that, but I'm a man*. I f...ed up, right? I gave an idiot a chance to make a name for himself, but that's fine. Now, Nestor, at least I'll sleep with a clear conscience. You, with your dirty tricks, you won't. Because this rule is meant to combat racism, not for you to use to your advantage."Neymar's response made clear how strongly he objected to the decision, but his accusation that Nestor had faked the incident remains his own claim. The controversy also has consequences beyond the match: Neymar will miss Santos' next fixtures against Palmeiras and Red Bull Bragantino, having already incurred a suspension through his yellow-card accumulation before receiving the red.The episode leaves a difficult question for football officials: how can rules designed to expose and deter discriminatory abuse be enforced fairly when the words exchanged between players cannot readily be heard? In Neymar's case, the referee's decision was clear. The competing accounts of what was said, however, remain at the heart of the controversy.
Article Summary: Neymar was sent off in Santos’ 1-1 draw with Bahia after covering his mouth during a heated exchange with Rodrigo Nestor. It followed an earlier confrontation between the pair and a half-time television interview in which Nestor accused Neymar of disrespecting him and Bahia. The Brazilian forward later admitted he had made a mistake but fiercely accused his opponent of exploiting an anti-racism measure to gain an advantage.

Article Title: FIFA U15 World Cup 2026: India beat Cameroon 2-1, register second consecutive Group K win
Article Text:
Baku, Oct 25 (IANS) India continued their winning start at the inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup 2026, defeating Cameroon 2-1 in their second Group K match at the Hovsan Competition Complex Pitch 1B on Sunday.

Jenit shines as India withstand Cameroon pressure

Lalremruatfela scores winner as Jenit saves penalty

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India continued their impressive start at the inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup 2026, beating Cameroon 2-1 in their second Group K match on Sunday. The Blue Colts took an early lead through a Cameroon own goal, but Muhammad Sohil Khan’s own goal brought the African side level before the break.Captain R Lalremruatfela scored the winner in the second half, finishing a low cross from Deepak Singh Arambam. Goalkeeper Jenit Ningthoujam played a key role in the victory, making several important saves, including stopping a penalty.With two wins from two matches, India are the only team in Group K to have won both their games so far.India got off to a quick start in rainy conditions when Deepak’s corner in the first minute led to Fareil Ngobo accidentally putting the ball into his own net. Cameroon gradually grew into the game, but India defended well and created chances to extend their lead.Goalkeeper Jenit was particularly impressive, denying several Cameroon attempts, including a dangerous free-kick and a close-range effort. India also came close to scoring through Lalremruatfela, but Cameroon managed to clear the danger.Cameroon eventually equalised in the 20th minute when Ndam Moctar’s cross struck Muhammad Sohil Khan and went into the net.The teams went into the break level at 1-1.India came out with greater purpose after half-time, and substitute Ronandev Aheibam made an immediate impact by winning the ball in midfield. He passed it wide to Deepak, who sent a low cross into the box. Lalremruatfela calmly finished with his left foot in the 27th minute to put India back in front.Cameroon had a chance to equalise after being awarded a penalty for handball, but Jenit came to India’s rescue once again, saving Harouna Abdoulaye’s spot-kick in the 32nd minute.India continued to threaten, with Ronandev testing the Cameroon goalkeeper and Soumojit Sarkar forcing another save from a free-kick. The Blue Colts held their lead until the final whistle, securing their second consecutive win and strengthening their position in Group K.
Article Summary: India beat Cameroon 2-1 in their second Group K match on Sunday. The Blue Colts took an early lead through a Cameroon own goal. Muhammad Sohil Khan’s own goal brought the African side level before the break. Captain R Lalremruatfela scored the winner in the second half.

Article Title: El Clasico preview: Barcelona’s goal machine meets its biggest test yet
Article Text:
Soccer Football - UEFA Champions League - Galatasaray v FC Barcelona - Rams Park, Istanbul, Turkey - October 13, 2026 FC Barcelona's Anthony Gordon celebrates scoring their third goal with Rodri REUTERS/Dilara Senkaya

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

(Watch El Clasico exclusively on FanCode at 1.30 am)

It’s still not Nov but there’s already a sense of inevitability around the La Liga season. Barcelona have been a free-scoring beast, winning all their nine games in emphatic fashion and are already six points clear of Real Madrid, who are still getting used to Jose Mourinho’s ways.A victory at Camp Nou on Sunday in the season’s first Clasico will hand Barcelona a runaway lead. Given the way the season has progressed so far, it could well be game, set and match.English winger Anthony Gordon, in his first season for the Catalan giants, has been one of the important cogs in the wheel. Though he has scored only once in the Liga so far, the mild-mannered attacker has been a livewire down the left.When TOI asked him ahead about the secret sauce behind Barca’s indomitable goal-scoring spree this season, the winger said, “It’s a mix of the ability of some incredible players and having a relentless mindset to keep going. When we’ve been three, four goals up, we haven’t stopped attacking and our need and want for goals never went down. That reflects in the number of goals we’ve scored,” Gordon, who has fitted in well to coach Hansi Flick’s high-press attacking system, said.The 25-year-old was part of a Newcastle United team that put up a good fight in the first leg of the Champions League round-of-16 last season before being routed 2-7 at Camp Nou.But the Spanish champions are looking deadlier this season and Gordon attributes that to “players coming into their own”.“They’re showing a lot of character and personality. Lamine (Yamal) has gone to a different level, even Pau Cubarsí. The likes of Marc Bernal and Javi Espart are also really taking a step into the team. We have a very young team and for someone like Rodri to come and really calm the team down with his football intelligence has been very important,” Gordon said.
Article Summary: Barcelona are six points clear at the top of La Liga. The Catalan giants face Real Madrid in the season's first Clasico on Sunday. English winger Anthony Gordon has been a key player for Barca this season. Gordon attributes Barca's success to 'incredible players and a relentless mindset'

Article Title: Indian Super League: Ajaraie misses last-gasp penalty as Odisha hold NEUFC
Article Text:
(From left) NEUFC's Allaeddine Ajaraie and Jithin MS in action with Odisha FC's Stephen Eze at Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar on Saturday (Photo credit: NEUFC)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: It was almost an encore of their Indian Super League opener as NorthEast United once again looked set for a very late win on Saturday as Odisha FC defender Stephen Eze conceded a penalty in the fifth minute of injury time.However, contrary to expectations, Alaaeddine Ajaraie’s spot kick beat goalkeeper Hrithik Tiwary but not the woodwork as the match at Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar ended in a goalless draw.It was, in fact, a fair result for the eighth-paced Juggernauts, who got their first point of the season, and their impressive defence, as the Highlanders failed to continue their winning run even as the point took them to the top of the table with seven points from three matches.The match began as a tactical battle between the coaches with TS Purushothaman resorting to a strong defensive shape that the hosts have been more used to over the seasons, with three centre-backs – Jeremy Zohminghlua, veteran Eze and Thoiba Singh Moirangthem – inside the six-yard box.It was a perfect answer to Juan Pedro Benali’s tactic of quick attack with Ajaraie in a more central role in combination with Nikola Ninkovic and aided by Jithin MS and Macarton Nickson from the wings.Jithin, who scored the winner in their opener against the mighty Mohun Bagan Super Giant, created the first NEUFC attack as early as in the third minute with a run from the right wing and beating a persistent Jeremy to send in a ball at the centre. But Odisha’s young custodian Hrithik Tiwary stood tall to parry the shot from Ninkovic towards safety.Ajaraie, away from his conventional position in the flanks, made a few impressive runs throughout the first half, especially in the 23rd and 28th minutes, down the middle, but after dodging and nutmegging the defenders, failed to produce the finish that his Spanish coach hoped for from the sidelines.Odisha, on the other hand, depended on counter-attacks as Everton Nascimento, Mahmoud Eid and K Lalrinfela waited in the opposition half to find a breakthrough.The best chance of the half came to Antonio Moyano in the 45th minute but, with only Tiwary to beat, he shot the ball too high to make a difference.Although devoid of a goal, the match continued to be an exciting affair with a proactive Jithin and skilful Ajaraie used all tricks in their bag to get past the Odisha defence. There were also physical duels, like the ones involving the young Blue Tigers and Highlanders attacker Pramveer Singh and Odisha skipper Lalthathanga Khawlhring or ‘Putieia’ in the middle.However, the scoreline stayed unchanged even as the ends were changed and both coaches brought in reinforcements.Even as the NEUFC attacks continued, with Ajaraie and Ninkovic coming very close to scoring throughout the second half, Everton and Eid combined near the NEUFC goal with some impressive moves, together with substitute Rahim Ali, only for the hard-working Nikhil Barla at the back and Gurmeet Singh in goal coming to NEUFC’s rescue.That was until the 95th minute of the match when all the hard work from Odisha looked to have been put paid by the outstretched hand of Eze inside the box.However, it was not to be as the right post saved Ajaraie’s penalty kick and Odisha’s day in front of the home crowd.
Article Summary: Odisha FC defender Stephen Eze conceded a penalty in the fifth minute of injury time. Alaaeddine Ajaraie’s spot kick beat goalkeeper Hrithik Tiwary but not the woodwork. The match at Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar ended in a goalless draw.
